classification.difficultyReason: Proves a conditional-probability identity using a set intersection and mutual exclusivity.

content.prompt:
If $A$ and $B$ are mutually exclusive events, show that
$$P(A\mid A\cup B)=\frac{P(A)}{P(A)+P(B)}.$$

answer.short:
$A\cap(A\cup B)=A$ and $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)$, so
$$P(A\mid A\cup B)=\frac{P(A)}{P(A)+P(B)}.$$
answer.worked:
Since $A\subseteq A\cup B$, we have $A\cap(A\cup B)=A$. Mutual exclusivity gives $P(A\cap B)=0$, so $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)$.

Provided $P(A\cup B)>0$, the conditional-probability formula gives
$$\begin{align*}P(A\mid A\cup B)&=\frac{P(A\cap(A\cup B))}{P(A\cup B)}\\P(A\mid A\cup B)&=\frac{P(A)}{P(A)+P(B)}.\end{align*}$$
